title: Organic Chemistry: Polymers - Worksheet 5
topic: Addition and Condensation Polymerisation, Polyesters, and Polyamides
subject: Pure Chemistry

questions.question: Which statement best defines the term polymer?
options: A small, highly reactive molecule containing a single covalent bond
A macromolecule built up from many small repeating units called monomers
A giant lattice structure composed entirely of oppositely charged ions
A mixture of different hydrocarbon fractions with identical boiling points
questions.explanation: Polymers are large macromolecules formed by linking thousands of small molecular units called monomers together.

questions.question: During the formation of poly(ethene) from ethene monomers, what type of polymerisation reaction takes place?
options: Condensation polymerisation
Substitution polymerisation
Addition polymerisation
Hydrolysis polymerisation
questions.explanation: Poly(ethene) is formed via addition polymerisation, where unsaturated ethene monomers join together without the loss of any other atoms or small molecules.

questions.question: Which of the following is a necessary structural feature for monomers to undergo addition polymerisation?
options: They must contain at least one reactive carbon to carbon double bond
They must have a dicarboxylic acid functional group at both ends
They must be completely saturated hydrocarbon molecules
They must possess an amino functional group and a hydroxyl group
questions.explanation: Addition polymerisation requires unsaturated monomers containing carbon to carbon double bonds (C=C), which open up to form single bonds linking the polymer chain.

questions.question: How does the total mass of the polymer product compare to the total starting mass of the monomers in a pure addition polymerisation reaction?
options: The total mass decreases because gas molecules are released
The total mass increases because oxygen atoms add to the chain
The total mass remains exactly the same
The total mass doubles due to the formation of cross links
questions.explanation: In addition polymerisation, monomers simply join together to form the polymer without losing any atoms, meaning mass is fully conserved and remains the same.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a defining feature of condensation polymerisation?
options: Monomers react together with the elimination of a small molecule such as water
Only monomers with carbon to carbon double bonds can react
The polymer formed has a lower relative molecular mass than the monomers
It can only take place inside a vacuum at low temperatures
questions.explanation: Condensation polymerisation involves the linking of monomers with the simultaneous loss of a small molecule, most commonly water (H₂O) or hydrogen chloride (HCl).

questions.question: What pair of functional groups must react together to produce a synthetic polyester chain?
options: A dicarboxylic acid and a diamine
A dicarboxylic acid and a diol
An alkane molecule and an alkene molecule
A dialkali solution and a disulfate compound
questions.explanation: Polyesters are formed when dicarboxylic acid monomers react with diol monomers, creating ester linkages throughout the macromolecule.

questions.question: Which of the following is a widely used artificial polyester mentioned in your syllabus?
options: Nylon
Poly(ethene)
Terylene
Protein
questions.explanation: Terylene is a well known synthetic polyester built from ester linkages, used extensively in textiles and clothing fibers.

questions.question: What is the structural formula representing an ester linkage inside a polyester molecule?
options: –CONH–
–COO–
–C=C–
questions.explanation: An ester linkage consists of a carbonyl group bound to an oxygen atom, represented structurally as –COO–.

questions.question: To form the synthetic polyamide known as Nylon, which two monomer functional groups are required to react?
options: A dicarboxylic acid and a diol
A diol and a diamine
A dicarboxylic acid and a diamine
An alkene monomer and a dicarboxylic acid
questions.explanation: Nylon is a synthetic polyamide formed through condensation polymerisation between dicarboxylic acid monomers and diamine monomers.

questions.question: What is the name of the linkage that joins the repeating units together in a polyamide like Nylon?
options: Ester linkage
Amide linkage
Glycosidic linkage
Double covalent linkage
questions.explanation: Polyamides are defined by the presence of amide linkages (–CONH–) which hold the monomer units together.

questions.question: Which of the following macromolecules is a natural polyamide found in living organisms?
options: Terylene
Nylon
Protein
Starch
questions.explanation: Proteins are natural polyamides. They are built up from amino acid monomers linked together by amide linkages, which are biologically referred to as peptide bonds.

questions.question: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins. What functional groups must every amino acid monomer contain to form a natural polyamide?
options: An amine group and a carboxylic acid group
An alcohol group and an alkene group
A carboxylic acid group and an alcohol group
An amine group and an alcohol group
questions.explanation: Amino acids are bi functional molecules containing both an amine group (–NH₂) and a carboxylic acid group (–CO₂H), allowing them to polymerise into natural polyamides.

questions.question: How do the structural linkages of Nylon and natural proteins compare to one another?
options: Nylon contains ester linkages, while proteins contain amide linkages
Nylon contains amide linkages, while proteins contain ester linkages
Both Nylon and proteins contain identical amide linkages joining their monomer units
Nylon is an addition polymer, while proteins are polyesters
questions.explanation: Both synthetic Nylon and natural proteins are polyamides, meaning they are both structurally held together by the same type of amide linkages (–CONH–).

questions.question: If 100 monomers react completely to form a single continuous condensation polymer chain, approximately how many small water molecules are eliminated?
options: Exactly 50
Exactly 100
Approximately 99 or 100
Zero molecules
questions.explanation: Each linkage formed in a condensation polymerisation reaction eliminates a small molecule. Linking 100 monomers together creates around 99 to 100 links, freeing a matching number of water molecules.

questions.question: What chemical process can break down a synthetic polyester or a natural protein back into its individual monomer components?
options: Addition polymerisation
Acid catalysed hydrolysis
Physical melting
Fractional distillation
questions.explanation: Depolymerisation of polyesters or polyamides can be achieved via hydrolysis (reaction with water), which is typically accelerated using an acid catalyst.

questions.question: A fiber sample is tested and found to contain natural ester bonds that form a complex network. Which classification does this material fall under?
options: Natural polyamide
Natural polyester
Artificial polyamide
Artificial addition plastic
questions.explanation: A material containing naturally occurring ester bonds belongs to the group of natural polyesters, distinct from synthetic polyesters like Terylene.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary environmental problem associated with the disposal of non biodegradable synthetic plastics like poly(ethene)?
options: They dissolve rapidly in rainwater, making lakes acidic
They accumulate in landfills and oceans because decomposers cannot break them down easily
They release oxygen gas that accelerates atmospheric warming trends
They react with nitrogen gas to create toxic ammonium clouds
questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable plastics do not get broken down by natural decomposers, leading to severe environmental accumulation, marine hazards, and landfill overcrowding.

questions.question: What happens during the chemical recycling method of plastic depolymerisation?
options: Plastics are shredded and melted directly into small physical pellets
Polymers are chemically broken down into their individual original monomers
Plastics are compressed into solid composite building blocks for construction
Polymers are mixed with sulfur to increase their elasticity properties
questions.explanation: Chemical recycling via depolymerisation breaks the bonds within the polymer chain to recover the starting chemical monomers, which can be reused as a fresh chemical feedstock.

questions.question: Which of the following lists a typical everyday use for the synthetic polyamide Nylon?
options: Disposable food wrappers and clingfilm
Fishing lines, parachutes, and sleeping bags
As an alkaline solution to neutralize acid soils
As a fuel feedstock for heavy industrial furnaces
questions.explanation: Due to its high strength, elasticity, and durability, Nylon is widely manufactured into items like clothing, fishing lines, curtains, and parachutes.

questions.question: A polymer chain snippet shows a repeating sequence of alternating dicarboxylic acid blocks and diol blocks. Identify this polymer class.
options: Addition polymer
Polyamide
Polyester
Natural polyunsaturated fat
questions.explanation: An alternating chain of dicarboxylic acids and diols establishes regular ester linkages, classifying the substance as a polyester.
